## Intent
Hypothesis: scalar, non-vectorized processing with simple loop structure is compute/overhead-bound rather than bandwidth-bound on branchy-respawn particle workloads.

## Cache saturation
All measured N (4000–4M) exceed the L1d spill (N≈963); the L2 spill at N≈61680 falls between N=16000 and N=65000. At q=0.01, ns/p goes 8.078 (N=16000) → 7.912 (N=65000, just past spill) → 7.811 (N=1M) — cost FALLS slightly through L2→DRAM with no knee. The curve is FLAT across N at every death rate, with mild overhead amortization at small N (8.364 at N=4000 → 7.811 at N=1M). Death rate raises the floor without changing the N-shape: q=0.01 ≈7.8, q=0.05 ≈8.5, q=0.25 ≈11.1 ns/p. No cache-spill knee appears anywhere.

## Bandwidth
Peak is 8.71 GB/s at N=1M, q=0.01 — 34.5% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling. At q=0.05, 7.97 GB/s (31.6%); at q=0.25, 6.11 GB/s (24.2%). The algo is overhead/compute-bound: never exceeds 35% of ceiling at any N or death rate, with no transition to bandwidth-bound behavior. Death rate is the primary lever — each 5× increase in q adds ~0.7 then ~2.6 ns/p, reflecting branchy respawn and scatter cost rising with churn. The slight BW improvement from N=4000 to N=1M is overhead amortization, not a regime change.

## Assembly
The compiler did not vectorize: 1 vector-suffixed instruction in 302 (`movi.2d v10, #0`, register zeroing). All FP work is scalar — `ldr s0`, `fmul s1, s1, s8`, `fadd s0, s0, s1`, `fcmp s0, s12`. No gather (no `ld1`). The scatter/deposit is byte-granular: `ldrb w2, [x1]`, `csel w2, w2, w11, lo`, `strb w2, [x1]` — 19 `strb`, 12 `ldrb`. Heavy control flow (21 `b`, 19 `cmp`, 18 `csel`, 6 `ccmp`, 4 `tbnz`) plus `udiv`/`msub` and 3 `bl` calls confirm branchy de-vec control. Scalar codegen with byte scatter explains the 34.5%-of-ceiling cap: the loop is instruction-count-bound, not memory-bound.

## Verdict
Holds — the scalar implementation is overhead/compute-bound, not bandwidth-bound. It sustains at most 8.71 GB/s = 34.5% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling (N=1M, q=0.01) with no cache-spill knee across N=4000–4M. Death rate raises the floor from 7.8 to 11.1 ns/p (q=0.01→0.25) without changing the flat N-shape, confirming branchy-respawn cost dominates over memory-system effects. The codegen — 1 vector instruction in 302, scalar `fmul`/`fadd`, 19 `strb` byte-scatter stores — explains the gap.
